# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

#### Static Assertions (Compile-time Testing)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
    
    // For traits and template metaprogramming
    STATIC_CHECK(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Point>);  // v3.0.1+
}
```

#### Conditional Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();
    
    // These record the expression but don't count as test failures (v3.0.1+)
    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value > 0
        REQUIRE(value <= 100);
    } CHECKED_ELSE(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value <= 0  
        REQUIRE(value >= -100);
    }
}
```

#### Benchmarking (v2.9.0+)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance testing", "[Benchmark]") {
    // Simple benchmarking
    BENCHMARK("Algorithm performance") {
        return expensive_algorithm();
    };
    
    // Advanced benchmarking with setup
    BENCHMARK_ADVANCED("Advanced benchmark")(Catch::Benchmark::Chronometer meter) {
        std::vector<int> data = setup_test_data();  // Setup not measured
        
        meter.measure([&] { 
            return process_data(data);  // Only this is measured
        });
    };
}
```

## OrcaSlicer-Specific Testing Patterns

### Geometry Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Line operations", "[Geometry]") {
    Line line{{100000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    Line parallel{{200000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(line));
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(parallel));
    
    // Test with epsilon tolerance
    Line rotated(parallel);
    rotated.rotate(0.9 * EPSILON, {0, 0});
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(rotated));
}
```

### Configuration Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Config loading", "[Config]") {
    DynamicPrintConfig config;
    std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_config/sample.ini";
    
    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(config.load_from_ini(config_path));
    REQUIRE(config.has("layer_height"));
}
```

### File I/O Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("STL file parsing", "[FileFormat]") {
    std::string stl_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_stl/20mmbox.stl";
    
    TriangleMesh mesh;
    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(mesh.ReadSTLFile(stl_path.c_str()));
    REQUIRE(!mesh.empty());
    REQUIRE(mesh.volume() > 0);
}
```

### G-code Generation Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("G-code writer functionality", "[GCodeWriter]") {
    GCodeWriter writer;
    
    // Load test configuration
    std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/fff_print_tests/test_config.ini";
    writer.config.load(config_path, ForwardCompatibilitySubstitutionRule::Disable);
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

lines: - **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.

- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.

- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
-- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **Ask AI may only read.**

+- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **The two buttons differ only in the sentence**: Ask AI and Resolve with AI send the same context and the turn gets the same tools.
- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.

- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** or **Resolve with AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.

- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Second run of the "persistent print issues" spike (2026-10-08). Kenneth called the first run (Codex, `investigation-persistent-print-issues.md` in the main checkout, producer hooks in Plater.cpp) "really bad" without saying why, and asked for an independent redo with a prototype pre-approved.

**Where it lives:** landed on `jusprin-newui` as `6394191523` on 2026-10-10 (cherry-picked in the main checkout after the same tree was built and tested on top of `2d5178581c`; not pushed by me). It was developed in worktree `.claude/worktrees/wonderful-roentgen-83d009`, whose branches `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1` (old base) and `claude/print-issues-on-newui` (tested copy) are now redundant. Report: `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md` there, evidence in the folder of the same name. Code: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/` (PrintIssueMonitor, IssueOverlay), `AgentHost::submit_issue_message`, harness modes `--print-issues`, `--print-issues-capture <dir>`, `--manual-print-issues`.

**Result:** end to end works with 0 lines changed in OrcaSlicer-owned files for the feature itself. The reader re-asks native checks instead of recording at producers.

**2026-10-09: converted to production work by Kenneth** ("ignore everything that said this is a temporary spike"). His decisions: hide ALL native notices; status pill in the canvas's lower right corner (where notices were), list opening upward; chat message quotes Orca's text. Upstream footprint is 2 added lines in `NotificationManager::render_notifications`: an early return when `wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden()` (Kenneth's idea: reuse the flag the shell already sets and restores; my first version added a 6-line dedicated switch). It asks the Prepare canvas, not the drawn canvas, because Check print is a second canvas without the flag and drew the notices again (tested). It sits after `sort_notifications()` because current upstream added `m_imgui_ready = true` at the top of the function (the merge simulation caught that). With no agent set up, a press sends nothing and a dialog offers setup (Kenneth's decision, 2026-10-09). A task chip was spawned for the four gaps hiding all notices leaves (operation notices, flushing-volume warning, future upstream warning kinds, readers never triggered at runtime). Uncommitted candidate passes: print-issues scenario 39 steps/336 checks in light and dark, shell regression 527, agent_bridge_tests 4756, jusprin_tests 584. Files no longer carry "spike" in their names: `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc`, `print_issues_agent.hpp`, `tests/jusprin/test_print_issues.cpp`.

Kenneth caught by hand that the bubble covered its object near the top edge; 324 green checks had missed it because nothing asserted "does not cover the object". Placement is now `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout` with unit tests.
--
**2026-10-10: the four gaps investigated** in worktree `.claude/worktrees/blissful-dhawan-1561d5` (report `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps.md` and folder of the same name, untracked; harness mode `--print-issue-readers`, steps chosen with env `JUSPRIN_READER_STEPS`). Facts worth not rediscovering: `PartPlate::check_tpu_printable_status` always returns true; OrcaSlicer trims a brim at the plate edge and at a nozzle's reach, a skirt is what puts a path outside; H2D has `machine_tool_change_time` 5.6 so OrcaSlicer's PLA+PETG warning never fires there (use X1C 0.4); a too-tall object is blocked before slicing, so the post-slice height readers stayed unverified; filaments must be switched on in AppConfig `filaments` and presets reloaded before `SetupCommands::compatible_filaments` lists them; `PlaterWarningNotification::close()` only hides and relies on the end of `render_notifications` to delete, so an early return there leaks hidden warnings that block re-pushes of the same text. Proposed, awaiting Kenneth: a 9-line `for_each_notification` accessor (serves operation notices, the flushing warning and a catch-all), an exhaustive switch over `NotificationType` as a build-time guard, and four defects in the candidate (blocker label disagreeing with Orca's ready-to-print test inside the 2 mm tolerance, the draw-suppression tail, nozzle-reach issues without an object, nozzle-area wording).

**2026-10-10: feature committed** by Kenneth as `6394191523` on `jusprin-newui` (so the wonderful-roentgen worktree is no longer the only home of the code). The four-gaps worktree was fast-forwarded onto it; all reproductions and the four merge simulations were redone there with the same results (commit objects: accessor `c5ef7a8157`, public flushing check `059bd32816`, hook `be0a9f45ff`, draw-loop variant `8bd274cc02`). The prototype is one file, `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps/prototype.patch`. The commit's 42-step `--print-issues` scenario passes with the draw-loop variant.

**2026-10-10 evening: feature taken off `jusprin-newui`.** Kenneth: "We will have to rethink the design." The commit `6394191523` now lives only on `feature-popup-message-handling` (local and origin); `jusprin-newui` was rebuilt as `2d5178581c` + the two later commits (`decf94b262`, `15907e82e3`), with `backup/jusprin-newui-before-drop` at the old tip `0fdc9c214f`. Verified: new tip's tree equals the old tip with the feature reversed, it builds, agent_bridge_tests 4677 / jusprin_tests 518 / shell scenario 529 pass. Branches `claude/determined-lovelace-636b05` and `codex/deferred-agent-tools` still sit on the feature commit. Do not treat the print-issues design or my four-gaps proposals as accepted; they are input to a redesign.

**2026-10-12: redesign agreed with Kenneth ("popup message handling").** His five points plus two decisions he made the same day:
1. OrcaSlicer's notification list becomes the source of truth for what JusPrin draws (all messages, not only print problems). Read through the 9-line `for_each_notification` accessor.
2. One observer call at the end of `NotificationManager::update_notifications` tells JusPrin to look again (another agent's idea; it runs on canvas idle, not per frame, and not while the window is inactive).

content.content:
**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].
description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"
**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].
**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.

git add -u && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Give Ask AI the same tools as Resolve with AI; the buttons differ only in the sentence

The print-issue bubble's two buttons used to send different things. Ask AI
tagged its context with "intent": "explain", and the host then replaced the
turn's tool list with the read-only tools and refused any other tool call
with the error code "explain_only". Resolve with AI was an ordinary turn.

Now both buttons send the same context and get the same, ordinary tool list.
The only difference is the sentence the person is shown as having said:
"Explain this issue and my options." or "Help fix this issue." The overlay
passes that sentence straight through ShellController::submit_issue to
make_issue_message.

Removed:
- AgentHost::explain_only_turn, the read-only tool-list switch in
  make_agent_request, and the refusal in handle_agent_tool_call.
- The refusal parameter of ToolExecutionCoordinator::propose, which only
  that refusal used (the coordinator files are back to their state before
  print issues were added).
- The IssueIntent enum, intent_name, and the "intent" field of the
  print-issue context. Nothing else read the field: the page treats
  issueContext as opaque.
- The two agent bridge tests that proved the read-only list and the
  refusal, the resolve test that existed only as their contrast, and the
  shell-harness checks that Ask AI was offered read-only tools and that
  the context named an intent.

A repeated press of the same button with nothing changed is still one
message: the client message id now hashes the sentence together with the
issue id, where it used to include the intent name. The unit test now
checks that both buttons produce an identical context, and the harness
checks that the Ask AI turn keeps the ordinary tool set.

Line count: 60 added, 181 removed (net -121). Source code: 24 added, 75
removed. Tests: 35 added, 105 removed. One line of agent-docs changed.

Tested: agent_bridge_tests (4809 assertions), jusprin_tests (635
assertions), and the shell harness --print-issues scenario (480 checks,
0 failures), all on a Release build of this tree.
EOF
git log --oneline -1

# Ask AI and Resolve with AI now send the same thing except one sentence

Branch `claude/ask-ai-same-tools`, commit 80fd03b118. It is based on
origin/jusprin-newui at 20de313d92, which is one fast-forward commit past the
0f46943de2 named in the brief. The tool-deferral commit is still absent there.
Not pushed.

## Problem

When OrcaSlicer reports a print issue, the canvas shows a bubble with two
buttons. Ask AI used to put `"intent": "explain"` in the context JSON attached
to the user message. The agent host read that field, swapped the turn's tool
list for the read-only tools only, and refused any other tool call with the
error code `explain_only`. Kenneth wants both buttons to send the same tools
and differ only in the wording of the user message.

## What was removed

- `AgentHost::explain_only_turn`, the read-only tool-list swap in
  `make_agent_request`, and the `explain_only` refusal in
  `handle_agent_tool_call`.
- The `refusal` parameter of `ToolExecutionCoordinator::propose`, because that
  refusal was its only user. Both coordinator files now match their state
  before the print-issues commit d0bce03db3, byte for byte.
- The `IssueIntent` enum, `intent_name`, and the `"intent"` field of the
  print-issue context. The page never read the field, because `protocol.ts`
  types `issueContext` as `unknown`, so no page or vitest change was needed.
- Two agent bridge tests: one for the read-only tool list and one for the
  refusal. Also a third test whose only job was to contrast a resolve turn
  with that refusal, plus the shell-harness checks for read-only tools and
  for the intent field.

## Net line count

60 lines added and 181 removed, a net of -121. Source code: 24 added, 75
removed. Tests: 35 added, 105 removed. One line of
`agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` was reworded.

## What the two buttons send now

Both buttons call `ShellController::submit_issue(issue_id, sentence)`. The
overlay picks the sentence: "Explain this issue and my options." for Ask AI
and "Help fix this issue." for Resolve with AI. The user message is that
sentence followed by OrcaSlicer's own words as a quote. The attached context
is identical for both buttons: kind, issue, target, evidence, and workspace
session and revision. A unit test asserts that the two contexts are equal.
Both turns get the ordinary tool list.

Pressing the same button twice with nothing changed still produces one
message, because the client message id hashes the sentence together with the
issue id. Pressing the other button produces a new message.

## Tests

All runs used a Release build of this tree.

- agent_bridge_tests: 4809 assertions in 273 test cases, all passing.
- jusprin_tests: 635 assertions in 110 test cases, all passing.
- Shell harness `--print-issues`: 480 checks with 0 failures. The run includes
  `ask_turn_keeps_the_ordinary_tool_set` and
  `second_press_with_nothing_changed_adds_no_second_message`.

## Merge note

Another task is renaming `ToolExecutionCoordinator::propose` to `submit`
across the tree. This commit touches three lines that rename also changes:

- the `propose` call in `AgentHost::handle_agent_tool_call`;
- the `propose` declaration in `ToolExecutionCoordinator.hpp`;
- the `propose` definition in `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`.

On each line this commit drops the trailing `refusal` argument or parameter.
To resolve a conflict, keep the new name and drop the `refusal`.

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

- [jusprin-v2-poc rebase, not merge](jusprin-v2-poc-rebase-not-merge.md) — branch forks from release/v2.4; rebase only the fork's commits (2 conflicts) instead of merging upstream in (531).
- [Verify before claiming rebase risk](fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming.md) — three checks that would have caught three wrong confident claims in a fork audit.
- [Phase 1 shell wraps the intact Notebook](jusprin-shell-phase-1-design.md) — hide the tab strip, don't reparent Plater; sidebar policy seam; evidence doc location.
- [Inherited teardown crash](orca-inherited-teardown-crash.md) — exiting with volumes loaded segfaults in ~GLCanvas3D via destroyed Plater priv; predates the shell.
- [Worktree build recipe](jusprin-worktree-build.md) — cmake configure line reusing existing deps; use /Applications/CMake.app cmake, not Homebrew's; BUILD_TESTS=ON for tests; build jusprin_web explicitly after page edits or live runs use a stale prompt.
- [Agent bridge Phase 2](agent-bridge-phase-2.md) — bridge/page/protocol locations, npm bundle rebuild rule, availability toggle, deliberate gaps.
- [Agent bridge Phase 3](agent-bridge-phase-3.md) — ToolExecutionCoordinator, protocol v2 tool messages, staleness/idempotency semantics, deliberate gaps.
- [Agent bridge Phase 4](agent-bridge-phase-4.md) — persistence design, aux-dir healing rule, checkpoint suffix/GL traps, revert scratch-copy, benchmarks.
- [Agent bridge Phase 5](agent-bridge-phase-5.md) — attachments: capability (no version bump), blob storage + revert copy-forward, host decode/caps, native import seam, React composer, tradeoffs.
- [Protocol version only at compat boundary](protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary.md) — don't bump the bridge version for additive/pre-release changes; use the capabilities list.
- [Track wall-clock on background work](track-wall-clock-on-background-work.md) — verify long background tasks are progressing (ps CPU-time vs wall-clock); don't trust completion notifications.
- [Agent setup: API-key path](agent-setup-api-key-path.md) — verification-is-construction; the probe carries no project data; which setup routes are deliberately unbuilt.
- [Live-testing the built app on the Mac](live-test-built-app-on-mac.md) — shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance; "on another Space" usually means the second monitor; use the shell harness and an isolated $HOME.
- [zsh $VAR:path trap](zsh-var-colon-path-trap.md) — brace variables before a colon path (`${U}:path`) or git refs get mangled by history modifiers.
- [Bash cwd resets after background commands](bash-cwd-resets-after-background.md) — always `cd <worktree> &&` or use absolute paths; a wrong-dir build says "no work to do".
- [JusPrin rebrand seams](jusprin-rebrand-seams.md) — branch jusprin-rebrand: 3 seams + 1 attachment point, resource overlay for logos, build-time catalogs for the name, JusPrin2 key, what was left teal on purpose.
- [Report outcomes, not obstacles](report-outcomes-not-obstacles.md) — skip solved-problem narration unless it changes what Kenneth does.
- [Chip Orca seams](jusprin-chip-orca-seams.md) — bed type via the public set_bed_type_accord_combox; no public filament-preset call, compose the pieces.
- [Render widgets to a bitmap for visual proof](render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof.md) — 267 green checks hid two rendering defects; screen capture was unavailable.
- [Figma MCP seat limits](figma-mcp-view-seat-limit.md) — Dev seat on the Obico team since 2026-10-13 (200 calls/day); the old View-seat 20/month cap and its history; check whoami first.
- [Windows GUI test VM on GCP](windows-gui-test-vm-gcp.md) — headless Windows GUI testing works; four silent traps (Mesa/llvmpipe, Defender, session isolation, 640x480) and the fixes.
- [HeaderMenu closes before invoking](header-menu-closes-before-invoking.md) — row callbacks outlive the popup; controllers must be shared_ptr or the app crashes.
- [Agent panel CSS namespaces](agent-panel-css-namespaces.md) — styles.css is global; `setup-*` belongs to the setup screens, and a name clash breaks layout with all tests green.
- [Linux ARM build in Docker](linux-arm-docker-build.md) — all 25 deps compile on aarch64 in 45 min; reuse build_linux.sh -g's embedded Dockerfile, use a volume not a bind mount, GitHub 504 + Docker RAM gotchas.
- [Building JusPrin on the Windows VM](windows-build-on-gcp-vm.md) — full source build works; awk/scheduled-task/Eigen-artifact traps, and why Windows CI's failure is the runner, not the script.
- [Prove guard tests fail first](prove-guard-tests-fail-first.md) — Vitest returns CSS imports empty; inject the violation a lint-style test guards against and watch it fail before trusting it.
- [Fake Moonraker printer simulator](fake-moonraker-printer-sim.md) — lives on jusprin-newui-fakeprinter, NOT jusprin-newui; enable_ssl_for_mqtt=false or agent dials https.

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.

Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.

- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.

A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.

## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md

- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
